title: Silent Revision: Measuring Undisclosed Change in the Safety Frameworks of Frontier AI Developers
note: Primary source (item 1). Single author, Oxford Internet Institute. Comments field: under review at the AI & Science workshop (AISciK), NeurIPS 2026. Paper and data CC BY 4.0, code MIT. The 383/257/203 counts, the rates by direction, the eight pairs of Table 3 and the verbatim comparisons of Appendix F were all confirmed in this version.

title: frontier-safety-framework-corpus
note: Corpus and code repository named by reference 1 (item 2). Confirmed reachable (HTTP 200) at bibliography phase; repository contents were not opened for direct comparison.

title: The 2025 Foundation Model Transparency Index
note: Average score 40.69/100, down from 58 in 2024; highest IBM at 95; lowest xAI and Midjourney at 14 each. Checked directly by Pebblous (item 3).

title: Privacy Policies over Time: Curation and Analysis of a Million-Document Dataset
note: 1,071,488 English-language privacy policies across more than 130,000 websites, spanning over twenty years (item 4). The closest precedent for the corpus method; reference 1 adds a comparison axis this paper lacks — the developer's own account of the revision.

title: Evaluating AI providers' frontier safety frameworks
note: Snapshot assessment scoring twelve providers against 65 criteria (item 5). Also cited in the same item: Liang, W., Rajani, N., Yang, X., Ozoani, E., Wu, E., Chen, Y., Smith, D.S. & Zou, J. (2024), 'Systematic analysis of 32,111 AI model cards characterizes documentation practice in AI,' Nature Machine Intelligence 6:744-753, doi:10.1038/s42256-024-00857-z — field completeness across 32,111 model cards. Both citations and figures are carried over from reference 1 (Zhu 2026); Pebblous did not open either original.

title: Seeing without knowing: Limitations of the transparency ideal and its application to algorithmic accountability
note: Reference 1's starting point (item 6): the transparency ideal confuses seeing with knowing. Also cited in the same item, within the range reference 1 cites: Vaughan, D. (1996), The Challenger Launch Decision: Risky Technology, Culture, and Deviance at NASA, University of Chicago Press — structural secrecy; Meyer, J.W. & Rowan, B. (1977), 'Institutionalized organizations: Formal structure as myth and ceremony,' American Journal of Sociology 83(2):340-363, doi:10.1086/226550 — decoupling; Brunsson, N. (1989), The Organization of Hypocrisy: Talk, Decisions and Actions in Organizations, John Wiley & Sons — organised hypocrisy; Power, M. (1997), The Audit Society: Rituals of Verification, Oxford University Press — auditability as a property of how records are kept.

title: Senate Bill No. 53: Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act
note: Requires framework publication and, on any material modification, publication of the modified framework with a justification within thirty days; 'material modification' is undefined; effective 1 January 2026 (item 7). Also cited in the same item: European Commission, AI Office (July 2025), 'The General-Purpose AI Code of Practice,' https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/contents-code-gpai — requires signatories to update their framework at least annually and submit each update to the AI Office within five business days. Both described only within the range cited by reference 1 (Zhu 2026).

title: 21 CFR 314.70 — Supplements and other changes to an approved application
note: (a)(6): duty to include a list of all changes in a supplement or annual report. (b)(1): changes requiring a prior-approval supplement. (c)(6)(iii)(A): changes-being-effected-on-receipt path for adding or strengthening a contraindication, warning, precaution or adverse reaction. Pebblous checked the text of all three provisions directly (item 8), as of the current eCFR codification.

title: ISO 9001:2015 — Quality management systems — Requirements
note: §7.5.2 (creation and updating of documented information — identification and description) and §7.5.3 (control of documented information — obsolete versions) (item 9). Also cited in the same item: ISO/IEC 5259-3:2024, Data quality for analytics and machine learning — Part 3: Data quality management requirements and guidelines, https://www.iso.org/standard/81088.html — covered previously by Pebblous in 'The AI Safety Dossier Is Really a Data Lineage Record.'

title: 인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법 (Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Establishment of a Foundation of Trust)
note: Effective 22 January 2026 (item 10) — a different law on a different date from California's TFAIA, which took effect 1 January 2026.

title: AI Safety Watchtower
note: Continuously tracks the safety and security policy documents of sixteen companies (item 11). The body quotes founder Tyler Johnston and cites the companion Seoul Commitment Tracker, where no company scored above B- and six received a failing grade.
